answer: Each identity claims one anchor chain at an inlet and locks 70 credits as bond. It paints every tenth link saffron and files chain length and mark positions. An auditor recounts it from the link table and checks the saffron sequence fits one chain; a duplicate chain, wrong count, or reused saffron sequence forfeits the bond. First chain costs 24, the kth 24+8(k-1), the 1000th 8016; 1000 fakes cost 4,020,000 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-chain ring fails: reusing the same anchor chain's saffron sequence exposes the duplicate. An honest owner spends 24 once and regains the 70 after one epoch.
